Welcome to the seminar on infrastructure regulation. Some of you come from Brazil, some from Italy and some from Spain, so English is the language that we all share. Please don't worry about your accent. What I care about is precision. Every week, one student presents a case study which he or she has chosen. The presentation is short, fifteen minutes, and it must start with a clear definition of the problem. After that, the group discusses it. The students who participate most are not the ones with perfect English. They are the ones who come prepared, with a question.

I did the international part of my doctorate at a university in Madrid, where most of the classes were in English. The first month was difficult. I understood the texts, which I could read slowly at home, but I did not understand the discussions, which were very fast. My supervisor, who was very patient, gave me a simple tip. Before every class, read the abstract of each article twice, and write one question. It worked. After two months, I was the student who asked the first question in every class. My thesis, which I defended last year, is about precedent in energy regulation.
